correctness.rationale: Exact down-spin induced-edge counting gives U>=n+M and classifies equality by six compatible triangular-rung spin patterns. At fields 2J and 4J the six- and four-state transfer traces produce the claimed quadratic algebraic power sums. On 2J<h<4J the minimizers are independent sets with one down spin per rung, counted by proper cycle 3-colourings. At low field the odd-circumference obstruction and exact kink/isolated-rung enumerations yield the parity-specific counts. Independent exact 8-state min-plus checks cover 168 n/field combinations; direct full-spin checks cover 24. No extrapolation from finite checks is used as proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed contribution is the full finite-periodic classical nearest-neighbor Ising-tube field classification, not the known fact that frustrated three-leg geometries can exhibit plateaux or that transfer matrices solve finite-width classical models. The inspected full primary texts have different spin algebras/couplings or no field; the closest classical zigzag source has a different graph and was only accessible in abstract.

The cited published three-leg quantum spin-tube studies motivate the physics but do not certify historical priority of these exact Ising formulas.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact classification of a frustrated finite spin tube, not a single arbitrary finite table. It identifies a macroscopic one-third plateau degeneracy (entropy density ln(2)/3), parity-sensitive low-field counts (constant versus cubic), and two distinct algebraic critical field degeneracy rates. Such finite-size boundary effects and critical entropy rates are relevant to frustrated-ladder statistical mechanics.
